scholarships.title: Huayu Enrichment Scholarship (HES), Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan)
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Education (MOE), Republic of China (Taiwan)

existing.description: The Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) established the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship to encourage international students to study Mandarin Chinese in Taiwan. The award funds a 2-month summer course or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course, and pays a monthly stipend of NT$28,000. Applicants must be foreign nationals aged 18 or over with an excellent academic record and good moral character, must already have applied to a Chinese language centre, and must submit their documents to the ROC overseas office for their country of nationality. MOE publishes no single deadline date, noting only that applications are made 'before the deadline specified in the scholarship guidelines issued by that authorized overseas office (usually in January or February each year)'.
eligibility: A foreign person (not an ROC passport holder and not an overseas compatriot student).
Has graduated from secondary school or has studied at post-secondary level.
Excluded: a person currently studying Chinese in Taiwan, or who has previously undertaken a degree programme in Taiwan.
Excluded: a person who has previously received a Huayu Enrichment Scholarship, a TUSA Global Ambassador Scholarship, or a Taiwan Scholarship.
Excluded: an exchange student currently studying or researching in Taiwan under an academic cooperation agreement between a Taiwan university/college and an overseas institution.
Excluded: a person currently studying or researching in Taiwan who is receiving a scholarship or financial assistance from any Taiwan government agency or any educational institution in Taiwan.

Exception: the graduation and academic records of a foreign national recommended or selected by a foreign government, institution or educational institution under an education cooperation agreement are not subject to the preceding exclusion.
existing.eligibility_summary: Foreign nationals aged 18 or over who have graduated from secondary school or studied at post-secondary level, with an excellent academic record and good moral character. Excluded are overseas compatriot students and ROC passport holders, people currently studying Chinese in Taiwan or who previously completed a degree programme in Taiwan, people who previously received an HES, TUSA Global Ambassador Scholarship or Taiwan Scholarship, exchange students in Taiwan under a cooperation agreement, and people already studying or researching in Taiwan while holding another Taiwanese scholarship or financial aid.
benefits: Monthly stipend of NT$28,000 for the duration of the awarded course (2-month summer course, or 3, 6, 9 or 12 months).
coverage: No tuition, accommodation, airfare or insurance coverage is stated on the MOE HES page.
requirements: Meet the five published eligibility conditions and avoid all five published exclusions.
Have graduated from secondary school or studied at post-secondary level with an excellent academic record.
Have already applied to a Chinese language center, and supply proof of that application.
Submit all five required document types listed by MOE.
Apply before the deadline set by the relevant ROC overseas mission.
documents: A photocopy of the applicant's passport, or other documentation adequate proof of nationality
A photocopy of proof of the applicant's highest education level and photocopies of related transcripts
A photocopy of documentary proof that the applicant has already applied to a Chinese language center (for example, a photocopy of the application-for-admission form)
Any other documents required by the authorized overseas office handling the application
application_method: Submit the required documents and apply to the authorized overseas office in the applicant's country of nationality, or to the authorized overseas office with jurisdiction over Taiwan-related matters in that country.
Alternatively, where another method is required to facilitate the implementation of a policy, applications are not subject to being made this way.
Also apply separately to the chosen Mandarin Chinese language training center, and submit proof of that application as part of the package.
existing.selection_notes: The scholarships are awarded through Republic of China (Taiwan) embassies and overseas missions (Representative Offices) on the basis of merit, using the guidelines each office issues for its own jurisdiction.
existing.best_fit: Adults aged 18 or over, from any country other than Taiwan, who want to study Mandarin at a Taiwanese university-affiliated language centre and can apply to that centre separately; the 2-month summer course suits short-stay learners and the 3-12 month awards suit longer immersion.
existing.notes: Important provenance issue: the stored official_source_url for this record (https://english.moe.gov.tw/cp-24-16833-23C09-1.html) is MOE's Taiwan Scholarship Program page, a different award (tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NTD 40,000 per semester plus a monthly living allowance of NTD 15,000 or NTD 20,000). It does not document HES. The live HES page is https://english.moe.gov.tw/cp-24-24284-3ea37-1.html, recorded in research_notes.url_observed. Do not merge HES money figures with Taiwan Scholarship figures. An older MOE 'Study in Taiwan' brochure states an HES stipend of NTD 25,000, whereas the current MOE HES page states NTD 28,000; the current page is authoritative.
existing.duration: A 2-month summer course, or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course.
existing.application_period: Annual, with the deadline set by each applicant's own ROC overseas mission or representative office, which MOE says is 'usually in January or February each year'. The round for the current cycle has closed as of 2026-10-04; the next nominations are expected in January or February 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Applicants must apply to the authorized overseas office for their country of nationality 'before the deadline specified in the scholarship guidelines issued by that authorized overseas office (usually in January or February each year)'. MOE publishes no single fixed date, so no ISO deadline date can be recorded.
existing.program_type: Government non-degree language scholarship (Ministry of Education Huayu Enrichment Scholarship, awarded through ROC overseas missions on merit)

scholarships.title: Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP) - Ph.D. Scholarship and Stipend, Academia Sinica
scholarships.official_source: Academia Sinica (Taiwan International Graduate Program), in collaboration with partner universities

existing.description: The Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP), administered by Academia Sinica with partner universities, admits international students to fourteen English-taught Ph.D. programmes and pays a tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month for the first year, extendable for one further year for students who perform well. Academia Sinica also subsidises the difference between international and domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years, but students still pay the domestic tuition rate, stated as roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester for the remainder. Applications are submitted online between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8) with no application fee, and admission results are usually announced in late June or early July for enrolment the following fall.
eligibility: International applicant seeking admission to one of the fourteen TIGP Ph.D. programmes.
Must satisfy the general and programme-specific admission requirements published on the TIGP site for the chosen programme.
Must not already hold the degree level to which they are applying, per TIGP's general admission requirements.
existing.eligibility_summary: International applicants seeking admission to one of TIGP's fourteen English-taught PhD programmes. Admission is competitive and per-programme; applicants must hold a qualifying degree by enrolment and are advised to contact the TIGP Admission Office. No application fee is charged. Academic integrity is a core value of the programme and breaches can affect grades, stipend and academic standing.
benefits: Tax-free monthly stipend of NT$40,000 (NT$34,000 + NT$6,000) for the first year.
Stipend extended for one additional year for students who perform well.
International tuition surcharge fully subsidised for five consecutive years, leaving students at the domestic tuition rate.
Eligibility to apply separately for the Presidential Fellowship, Research Performance Fellowship, Rising Star Fellowship, PhD Supplemental Stipend Program and Travel Grants.
coverage: Tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month (NT$34,000 + NT$6,000) for the first year.
Stipend extended for one further year for students who perform well.
Academia Sinica subsidises the difference between international and domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years, so international students pay the same tuition as domestic students.
Separate TIGP awards available on top: Presidential Fellowship, Research Performance Fellowship, Rising Star Fellowship, PhD Supplemental Stipend Program and Travel Grants.
No travel, accommodation or insurance provision is stated in the core TIGP scholarship/stipend description; accommodation is budgeted separately by the programme.
requirements: Apply online through the TIGP application system between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8).
Meet the general admission requirements and the specific requirements of the chosen Ph.D. programme.
Select a thesis advisor before the end of the first year of study.
Uphold the academic integrity standards of Academia Sinica and the partner university.
Confirm tuition arrangements with the programme secretary, since the domestic tuition rate varies by partner university.
documents: Online application submitted through the TIGP online application system (no application fee).
Academic records for the qualification stated in the online application.
Documents specified by the individual PhD programme's own admissions page.
existing.english_requirement: The fourteen TIGP Ph.D. programmes are taught in English. No mandatory English test score is stated on the TIGP scholarship, tuition or admissions pages read on 2026-10-04.
application_method: Submit the application online through the TIGP online application system at https://tigp.apps.sinica.edu.tw/index.php between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8).
Choose one of the fourteen Ph.D. programmes and meet that programme's own admission requirements.
Contact the TIGP Admission Office (tigp@as.edu.tw) with programme or application questions.
existing.selection_notes: Admission is decided per Ph.D. programme. TIGP states that admission results are usually announced in late June or early July, and each programme publishes its own admission criteria and evaluation. A research proposal and interview requirements are set at programme level.
existing.best_fit: International master's holders seeking a funded, English-taught research PhD in Taiwan across the natural sciences, life sciences, medicine, geoscience, interdisciplinary neuroscience, AI and East Asian studies, who are willing to pay domestic-rate tuition themselves.
existing.notes: TIGP is not free tuition. Academia Sinica subsidises the international fee differential for five consecutive years, so students still pay domestic tuition, stated as roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester thereafter. Budgeted living costs given on the official site are approximately NT$5,000-14,000 per month for accommodation, NT$6,000-10,000 for food and NT$1,000-3,000 for study and personal requirements, so the NT$40,000 stipend is broadly adequate but not surplus. After the stipend period, support depends on the thesis advisor. TIGP also runs a separate Taiwan International Internship Program (TIIP), which is not part of this award.
existing.duration: PhD programme of three years. The stipend is paid for the first year and, for students who perform well, extended for one more year; after the scholarship/stipend allowance period, further financial support depends on the individual thesis advisor.
existing.application_period: Annual, 1 November to 1 February (GMT+8). TIGP posts a 'TIGP Application Announcement' each November (the 2026 one was published 2025-11-01). Admission results are usually announced in late June or early July, and admitted applicants enrol in the following fall semester.
existing.deadline_display: The TIGP Admission Office receives online applications 'from November 1st to February 1st every year' (GMT+8). The most recent cycle, for fall 2026 entry, closed at 1 February 2026 and admissions results were announced on 20 July 2026. No application announcement for the next cycle had been posted as of 2026-10-04, so no exact calendar date is recorded.
existing.program_type: Research-based doctoral scholarship programme administered by a research institute (Academia Sinica) with partner universities
